# SystemVerilog refusal register (ls-sv, schema sv-0.2)

This file answers three questions about the SystemVerilog tier of proglib (ls-sv): **what does it refuse today**,
**what is meant to be allowed later (and what has to exist first)**, and **what will never be allowed (and which principle says so)**.

It is generated from [`docs/sv-refusals.json`](sv-refusals.json) by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and checked against the code by
`python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check`: a tagged refusal in the extractor or the Lean code that is missing from the data, or a
listed tag that has disappeared from the code, fails the check. The svGolf-facing twin, for contestants and task authors, is
`svgolf/REFUSALS.md`, generated from the same data. It lives with the svGolf project (the golf branch), so the paths under `svgolf/`
cited in this file are absent from a checkout without it.

A refusal is a LOUD `Unsupported` node (extractor) or a loud process / expression / elaboration error (Lean) or a loader gate: the
design either loads with a defined meaning or it does not load. Nothing here is silently approximated. The long reasons live in the
per-topic documents linked at the end (`docs/sv-*.md`); this register is the index and the classification.

Register of the sv-0.2 SYMBOLIC tier: `extractors/sv/extract.py` in symbolic mode (the `load_design_sv2` path), the Lean side (`LeanModels/Sv`: Param2, Hier2, Ingest2, Probe2, RangeGuard2, CombGuard2, CombAlias2, Sem2, Comb2Proc, the `sv_structure` recognizer), and the loader gates. The svGolf checker's own restrictions are in `svgolf/REFUSALS.md` (the svGolf project, golf branch), generated from the same data. Snapshot: working tree of branch `svgolf-prep` on 2026-10-29, including the uncommitted round-6 work (`PortConn:net-width`, `ArraySel:partial-overhang`, `Select:partial-overhang`, `Select:wide-index`, `AlwaysComb:alias-read`); regenerate after the in-flight jobs land.

## How to read this register

Every construct the sv-0.2 tier does not accept is refused LOUDLY, never evaluated to a guess. Each row is one refusal tag (or a family of tags) with a measured trigger, the reason, where the code raises it, and its future. Marks: `†` = proposed by the register authors, not yet confirmed by Thomas; `(unverified)` = read from the source, not triggered by a run; a bare category without `†` is a recorded decision or a plain statement of today's behaviour.

### The four categories

| category | meaning |
|---|---|
| `refused-now` | refused loudly today and this is the intended behaviour at this version; no future is recorded |
| `later` | refused today and intended to be ALLOWED once a stated prerequisite is met (a proof obligation, a model extension, a checker stage, a measured benefit); the row names the prerequisite and, where recorded, the plan item |
| `never` | refused by principle and not to be allowed: no meaning can be given that is the same for the proof (ls-sv / slang) and the score (Yosys netlist), or it is not synthesizable hardware, or it would let the proved design differ from the scored one; the row names the principle |
| `refused-pending` | decided and in flight, not yet in the code (transitional): the row names the decision; the completeness check allows its tag to be absent and warns once it appears |

### Two scopes: the ls-sv tier and svGolf admission

The register classifies each refusal for the **ls-sv semantics tier** (the `category` of the row). The charter rules the tier's endgame to be
the whole specification, including the verification tier (classes, constrained randomization, assertions) and the full clause-4 scheduler
([docs/sv-charter.md](sv-charter.md) sections 6.3, 6.4, 6.6), so a construct can be `later` for ls-sv and still be unacceptable in a
**svGolf submission**, whose scored artifact is a combinational Yosys netlist. Where the two differ the row carries a second line
`svGolf: ...` (the field `svgolf` in the data). Delays, randomness, classes, strings and reals are the typical cases: `later` in the
semantics, `never` for a golf submission (principles `P-NO-TIME`, `P-SYNTHESIZABLE`).

### Principles behind `never`

| principle | statement |
|---|---|
| `P-SAME-PROGRAM` | Proof and score read ONE program: a construct the two frontends (slang for the proof, Yosys for the score) read differently, that slang rejects (decided 2026-10-31: "a good reason to reject"), or that Yosys cannot read, cannot be admitted. |
| `P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES` | No construct whose meaning is a synthesis-tool directive: pragmas, attributes, `ifdef SYNTHESIS / YOSYS, translate_off comments. |
| `P-NO-TIME` | No delays, timing, wall-clock or time-dependent behaviour in a combinational task: synthesis ignores them, so the proved (timed) behaviour and the scored netlist would differ. |
| `P-SYNTHESIZABLE` | Not synthesizable hardware, for a design task whose scored artifact is a gate netlist from Yosys `read_verilog -sv`: class declarations, dynamic memory (queues, dynamic and associative arrays), `string` variables and parameters, `real` variables, fork/join, program blocks. The frontend does not read them (measured by `harness/sv/tools_split_audit/yosys_frontend.py`; a constant `real` in a parameter expression IS read), so they are out of scope for now; revisit if a different synthesis frontend is adopted (decided 2026-10-31, about classes: a future synthesis frontend may change that). Host access (file I/O, system calls, DPI) is refused by its own policy, not by this principle. |
| `P-NO-SILENT-PICK` | The PIPELINE tools split (slang / ls-sv for the proof, Yosys for the score, Verilator and Xcelium as simulators give different values for the same text) and no consistent reading exists: refuse loudly, never decide for one side. A split in which only Icarus differs is not a refusal but a declared departure (decided 2026-10-31), and neither is one in which only Xcelium differs from LRM text that slang, Verilator and Yosys follow (decided 2026-11-01: `\a \v \f`). |
| `P-DETERMINISM` | A combinational result must be a function of the inputs, whatever the schedule: randomness is refused, and so is a design with no completed run (it never satisfies `Terminates2`). Where the LRM itself leaves the schedule open (IEEE 4.7) the ruling of 2026-10-31 is that the construct is to be modelled and the golfer proves the output the same in every process-atomic legal run, not that it is refused for that reason. A simulator-versus-synthesizer mismatch (self-reading `always_comb`: the LRM's answer is deterministic, the synthesizers compute another) is not that case. |
| `P-TRUSTED-BASE` | (added by the register authors, to confirm) The evidence a verdict rests on (checker, trusted statement, generated Goal, axiom set, toolchain) must not be changeable by the submission; a proof is accepted by the kernel from the allowed axioms alone. |
| `P-NO-HOST-ACCESS` | (decided 2026-10-31 for the READING of files; confirmed 2026-11-01 for the rest of the family: "Yes, don't allow this. It's not safe.") The SystemVerilog text of a submission cannot read or write host files, run programs, read the environment or call native code: the checker runs untrusted text on the organizer's machine (Yosys's read_verilog itself opens the file of a $readmemh). The Lean file of a submission is not scanned for it: it is CONTAINED, by the checker's sandbox around every process that runs submitted text (WP-S, 2026-10-31; known hole "Host access from the Lean file of a submission", mitigated). |

## Allowed later (ordered by expected value for svGolf tasks)

What a contestant is likely to want first comes first. Rank and reason are the register authors' estimate (`†`); the prerequisite is what has to exist before the refusal can be lifted.

| # | construct | why a task wants it | prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ForLoopStatement` | popcount, carry chains and parity trees written as loops (task ladder: popcount) | remaining prerequisite: broader loop state for effectful or nonliteral bounds [LOOPS] |
| 2 | `CallExpression (user function call in expression position)` | helper functions for bit tricks, parity and constant functions | remaining prerequisite: a 4-state rule (score/fourstate.py) for unassigned or multiply-written locals and general call-frame semantics [USERFN] |
| 3 | `LocalDecl (scoped block-local declaration)` | block-local temporaries in always_comb (static locals of a module-level always_comb are hoisted since WP-PROC L1; the remaining scoped forms load and retain a named LocalDecl refusal) | none for a static block local of a module-level always_comb (hoisted, WP-PROC L1), including closed literal/fill/parameter/enum initializers; proposed prerequisite for the rest (runtime/effectful initializers, automatic variables, generate scopes): a LocalDecl statement (scoped temporaries) in Stmt2 / PStmt [AGGR] |
| 5 | `CallExpression ($countones, $onehot, $left, array and enum methods)` | $countones and one-hot predicates for fixed-width packed signals (the banlist already treats these bit queries as +) | none for fixed-width `$countones`, `$onehot`, `$onehot0`, and numeric enum methods; proposed prerequisite: per-built-in lowering for parameter-dependent widths, `$left`, enum `name()`, and array methods [OPS] |
| 7 | `ConditionalStatement:Unique \| :Unique0 \| :Priority` | unique / priority in priority encoders and one-hot muxes | WP5: a violated unique / unique0 / priority claim becomes a run-time error on the settled state, forced by Terminates2 [WP5] |
| 8 | any edge-phase process (always_ff, always @(posedge clk), an async-reset block), even with a dead clock | registered, pipelined and multi-cycle designs (serial multiplier, iterative divider) | the sequential layer: ls-sv models clock edges; the `Unclocked` requirement goes then [SEQ] |
| 9 | `ConversionExpression:Explicit` | size casts such as `8'(a + b)` are common in golf code | per-point width and signedness rules for parameter-named and aggregate casts [FOLDS] |
| 10 | `PortSymbol:2state \| VariableSymbol:2state \| NetSymbol:2state \| NamedValueExpression:2state` | `int` / `bit` declared types for loop variables and flags | 2-state value semantics for remaining net/integer/aggregate declarations and width-aware boundary witnesses [AGGR] |

## The register

One section per group. Columns: tag, a measured trigger (`H:` = the body of `module t(input logic [7:0] a, b, input logic c, output logic [7:0] y); ... endmodule`), why, where the code raises it (`file:function`; `python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --where ID` prints current line numbers), and the status.

### Procedural statements

Loops, waits, disables, assignments in odd positions, local declarations. The extractor tags that are slang class names (`ForLoopStatement`, ...) are the symbolic tier's default tag for a statement it has no lowering for.

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ForLoopStatement` | H: always_comb begin y=0; for (int i=0;i<4;i++) y[i]=a[i]; end | Literal-bounded, source-pure single-iterator forms are unrolled in the extractor; parameter-dependent pure bounds and positive compound steps (literal or parameter-valued) are retained and expanded at each instantiation point. A comparison whose operands are not both signed `int`-class values is loud until the loop evaluator carries SystemVerilog's real comparison signedness. Effectful, multi-iterator, overflowing, and otherwise nonliteral forms remain loud. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: remaining prerequisite: broader loop state for effectful or nonliteral bounds [LOOPS] |
| `WhileLoopStatement / DoWhileLoopStatement` | H: always_comb begin int i; y=0; i=0; while (i<4) begin y[i]=a[i]; i=i+1; end end (and do..while) | Same as for loops; a data-dependent trip count is additionally not combinational hardware. | `extract.py:_convert_test_loop` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: as ForLoopStatement, statically bounded forms only [LOOPS] |
| `RepeatLoopStatement` | H: always_comb begin y=0; repeat (2) y = y + a; end | No loop semantics in the symbolic tier. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: as ForLoopStatement, constant repeat count [LOOPS] |
| `ForeverLoopStatement` | H: initial forever #5 y = a; | A non-terminating process is a time construct, not combinational logic. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the full scheduler (initial, # delays) of ruling 6.4 [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `ForeachLoopStatement` | H: logic [3:0] m [0:3]; always_comb begin y=0; foreach (m[i]) m[i]=a[3:0]; y=m[0]; end | Iteration over unpacked arrays; no loop semantics in the symbolic tier. | `extract.py:_convert_foreach_loop` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: loop semantics plus run-time-indexed unpacked arrays (AGGR) [LOOPS] |
| `WaitStatement` | H: initial begin wait (c) y = a; end | Level-sensitive wait is a time / scheduling construct. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `DisableStatement` | H: always_comb begin : blk y=a; disable blk; end | Early exit from a named block needs control flow the Sem2 statement model does not have. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: an early-exit (named block / disable) control-flow model in the Sem2 statement model |
| `EventTriggerStatement` | H: event e; always_comb begin y=a; -> e; end | Named events are simulation synchronisation objects. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the scheduler (R1): events are region objects [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `RandCaseStatement` | H: always_comb begin randcase 1: y=a; 1: y=b; endcase end | Randomised branch choice: not deterministic hardware. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: constrained randomization of the verification tier [VERIF]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-DETERMINISM |
| `PatternCaseStatement` | H: always_comb begin case (a) matches 8'd1: y=1; default: y=0; endcase end | Tagged-union / pattern matching has no model in Sem2; whether Yosys reads tagged-union patterns was not established. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: tagged unions in the symbolic tier [AGGR] |
| `ConditionalStatement:Unique \| :Unique0 \| :Priority` | H: always_comb begin unique if (c) y=a; else y=b; end (unique0, priority likewise) | Yosys reads the qualifiers as full_case / parallel_case don't-cares, so a violated claim scores 0 GE; v0 refuses and WP5 will encode the claim as a proof obligation. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: WP5: a violated unique / unique0 / priority claim becomes a run-time error on the settled state, forced by Terminates2 [WP5] |

### Processes, event controls and always blocks

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TimedStatement:DelayControl` | H: initial begin #1 y = a; end (inside always_comb the source is a slang error: InvalidStatement) | Delays are time. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt`, `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `TimedStatement:SignalEventControl (second wait inside a process)` | H: always_ff @(posedge c) begin y <= a; @(posedge c) y <= b; end | A second event wait inside a process is a multi-cycle sequential process. | `extract.py:_convert_stmt` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `TimedStatement:EventListControl` | H: always @(a or b) y = a; / always_ff @(posedge clk or posedge rst) ... / a three-event list | Plain `always` lists with one or more edge-qualified 1-bit identifiers are modelled by the retained timed event-list process; scalar identifier, equality/inequality, and logical `iff` guards are sampled at publication. Mixed sampled-expression/scalar lists remain loud because scalar-list and expression-list registrations are separate. Direct `always_ff` clock/reset lists, including packed sampled expressions and three or more event members, now use the expression registration; empty and unsupported-conditional forms remain loud. Since 2026-11-01 (WP-PROC E1) a LEVEL-sensitive list in the symbolic tier (`@(a or b)`, `@(a, b)`, `@a`: no edge term, no `iff`, plain signals) is an `always_comb` under R1 to R6 (see pr-implicit-event; R2: the list names every read). Edge lists and mixed lists keep the sequential-layer boundary. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the sequential layer (generic sensitivity lists) [SEQ] |
| `TimedStatement:ImplicitEventControl (always @*)` | H: always @* y = a; | A level-sensitive block that can infer a latch with no proc error in Yosys; its initial-x behaviour differs between tools. Since 2026-11-01 (WP-PROC E1) `always @*` / `@(*)` is an `always_comb` when R1 to R6 hold (docs/sv-proc-lowering.md): no edge/iff/delay/nonblocking, a 4-state input and no 2-state input (an `@*` block does not run at time zero), no latch (full assignment on every path), no read before assignment, no module signal read through a called function, no other writer of a target. A block that fails keeps this tag with the rule in its text. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: none for a block satisfying R1 to R6 (R3 is the 4-state rule for the initial x, enforced in the extractor); the residue is the shapes the rules refuse [LATCH4] |
| `SignalEventControl:BothEdges \| :None_` | H: always_ff @(edge c) y <= a; / always_ff @(c) / always @(c) ... | Plain timed `always @(signal)` is modelled through the retained any-edge registration; `always_ff @(signal)` and both-edge controls still lack the clocked edge contract. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block`, `extract.py:_convert_event_wait` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `SignalEventControl:iff` | H: always_ff @(posedge c iff f(en)) y <= a; | Plain timed `always`, positive- or negative-edge `always_ff` clocks, and both events of two-edge asynchronous-reset `always_ff` admit scalar guards, constant-index packed guards, ascending or descending dynamic packed part-select guards, concatenations, and constant replications of admitted parts, sampled when the adjacent edge is published; calls, aggregate selectors, and other unsupported guards remain loud. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `SignalEventControl:iff-reset` | H: always_ff @(posedge c or negedge rst_n iff f(en)); | Scalar `reset_iff` guards on active-low or active-high asynchronous reset events are retained and sampled at the reset edge; unsupported reset guard expressions remain loud under the same scalar vocabulary. | `extract.py:_sym_areset_process` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `SignalEventControl:clock` | H: always_ff @(posedge a) y <= b; (8-bit clock in the symbolic tier) | Timed `always_ff` now uses the sampled-expression register for packed vector and selected clocks, applying the edge rule to the expression's least-significant bit. The symbolic sv-0.2 clock contract remains a 1-bit identifier; timed guarded, real-valued, named-event, chandle, aggregate, and otherwise unsupported expressions remain loud. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the sequential layer [SEQ] |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:NoEventControl (zero-delay always)` | H: always y = a; / always_ff y <= a; | IEEE 9.2.2.1: an always procedure with no control for simulation time creates a simulation deadlock, and 9.2.2.4: always_ff contains one and only one event control. slang reports both as errors, Icarus refuses both, Xcelium hangs on `always y = a;` at run time and rejects `always_ff y <= a;`; Yosys and Verilator silently read `always y = a;` as a wire. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **never**: P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:NoEventControl (concurrent assertion)` | module-level `assert property (...)` or `cover property (...)` (slang reports them as procedural blocks) | Concurrent assertions have no process model. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: assertions of the verification tier [VERIF] |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:AlwaysLatch` | H: always_latch if (c) y = a; | A latch's initial value is x in IEEE but Yosys resolves a never-loaded latch to 0 (measured), so a 4-state rule is needed first. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: a 4-state rule for a latch's initial x in score/fourstate.py before ls-sv models always_latch [LATCH4] |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:Final` | H: final $display("x"); | final blocks run at simulation end only. | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `ProceduralBlockSymbol:initialized-variable \| :initialized-unknown` | logic [7:0] q = 8'd1; always_comb q = a; (also always_ff writing q) | IEEE 6.5 counts a declared variable initialization as a procedural assignment for the continuous-versus-procedural mixture rule only; whether an initializer is a process that 9.2.2.2 forbids next to an always_comb / always_ff writer is not stated (docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md item 5). Xcelium 24.03 rejects the design (MULAXX) on every variant measured; Verilator warns MULTIDRIVEN citing 9.2.2.2 on the whole-variable form (init_whole) and PROCASSINIT on the procedural write over an initializer; slang, Yosys and Icarus accept with identical values. The common FPGA idiom `logic q = 0; always_ff ... q <= ...` is refused too (a recorded over-refusal). | `extract.py:convert_procedural_block` | **never**: P-NO-SILENT-PICK |

### Declarations, types, ports and nets

`<X>:2state` is the catch-all reason for every declared type that is not 4-state (int, bit, real, string, event, chandle, mailbox, ...); `:type` is unpacked / dynamic / queue / associative / struct; `:signed` any signed declaration.

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ContinuousAssignSymbol:delay, NetSymbol:delay` | H: assign #1 y = a; / wire #1 w = a; | Net and continuous-assign delays are time. | `extract.py:convert_continuous_assign`, `extract.py:convert_net_sym` | **later**: the scheduler (R1) [R1]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-NO-TIME |
| `ContinuousAssignSymbol:strength` | H: assign (strong0, highz1) y = a; / assign (weak0, weak1) y = a; | A drive strength on a continuous assignment has no reading the tools share. Yosys 0.53 cannot read it at all (`read_verilog -sv`: syntax error, so the scored netlist does not exist); Icarus 12 applies it (a highz term drives z); Xcelium 24.03 ignores it on a variable (`*W,CAVSTR`, y = a); Verilator 5.042 accepts a strength without a high-impedance term and stops on `highz` (`Unsupported: highz strength`). The symbolic extractor used to admit it as a plain assignment, because `_continuous_assignment_has_strength` reads source bytes that only the M0 path loads (the M0 path keeps its own handling). The rule is the syntactic one: every strength-qualified `assign` is refused, taken from the syntax tree (`lower_proc.has_strength`); nets with a strength were already refused (`NetSymbol:net-z`, N2). | `extract.py:convert_continuous_assign` | **never**†: P-SAME-PROGRAM<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| `PortSymbol:2state \| VariableSymbol:2state \| NetSymbol:2state \| NamedValueExpression:2state` | real r; string s; event e; chandle; mailbox; semaphore; virtual interface; integer and aggregate 2-state declarations; parameter-dependent 2-state locals; | Fixed-width and parameter-dependent packed `bit` ports, fixed-width flat packed `bit` variables, a fixed packed struct made entirely of `bit` fields, and fixed predefined 2-state integer variables (`int`, `byte`, `shortint`, `longint`) enter the value tier and squash X/Z at their assignment boundary. This residual tag covers 2-state nets, `integer`/uncovered local forms, unpacked or mixed-state aggregate shapes, parameter-dependent locals, and non-hardware types whose storage or boundary rules are not represented. | `extract.py:convert_port_sym`, `extract.py:convert_var_sym`, `extract.py:convert_net_sym`, `extract.py:_convert_named_value_expr` | **later**: 2-state value semantics for remaining net/integer/aggregate declarations and width-aware boundary witnesses [AGGR]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `PortSymbol:signed \| VariableSymbol:signed \| NetSymbol:signed` | signed nets without the exact single-driver shape; signed unpacked array ports; parameter-dependent signed aggregates; signed values in width-changing conversions | Flat signed variables, one-driver signed wires, fixed root-signed packed structs, fixed packed-struct members, and fixed one- or multi-dimensional unpacked signed array variables and ports retain signedness through existing flat-vector cells. Signed nets without that driver shape, parameter-dependent aggregates, and width-changing signed conversions remain outside the admitted paths. | `extract.py:convert_port_sym`, `extract.py:convert_var_sym`, `extract.py:convert_net_sym` | **later**: none for fixed signed array variables and ports; parameter-dependent signed aggregate storage and exact width-changing signed conversions in Param2 / Sem2 remain to be defined [SIGNED] |
| `PortSymbol:type \| VariableSymbol:type \| NetSymbol:type \| NamedValueExpression:type` | input logic [7:0] a [2] (fixed integral unpacked port); logic [7:0] q[$]; q[int]; an unpacked struct variable; a tagged union; a parameter-dependent fixed array or a dynamic/aggregate read | Fixed finite one- or multi-dimensional integral unpacked variable ports, fixed one-dimensional input net ports, fixed one-dimensional output wire ports with zero or one plain driver per cell, and fixed one-dimensional internal wire arrays with zero or one plain driver per cell flatten to existing scalar cells. Undriven net cells retain their z initial value. One- and two-dimensional fixed integral array reads and writes with run-time selectors expand to mutually exclusive case-equality branches over those cells. Multi-driver output/internal net arrays still require driver resolution; dynamic / queue / associative types, unpacked structs, and parameter-dependent shapes remain outside the declared-type vocabulary. | `extract.py:convert_port_sym`, `extract.py:_convert_fixed_array_port_sym`, `extract.py:convert_var_sym`, `extract.py:convert_net_sym`, `extract.py:_convert_fixed_net_array_sym`, `extract.py:_convert_named_value_expr` | **later**: none for fixed integral variable ports, one-dimensional input net ports, zero/one-driver output wire cells, zero/one-driver internal wire cells, and fixed one- or two-dimensional array reads and writes; multi-driver net arrays, unpacked structs, parameter-dependent or dynamic storage and deeper aggregate shapes need their own layout and access semantics [AGGR]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |
| `VariableSymbol:tagged-struct` | a packed tagged union variable (the probe reported VariableSymbol:type instead) | Tagged unions are not modelled. | `extract.py:convert_var_sym` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: tagged unions in the symbolic tier [AGGR] (unverified) |

Fixed one-dimensional internal and output wire-array cells may also retain undriven cells as z-initialized storage when every driven cell has at most one plain driver. Still refused here: no driver or a partial cover on scalar/packed nets, two drivers on a bit, a driver in a generate scope, a net in a generate scope, windows of a parametric-width net, other net types, 2-state nets, and signed nets without the exact single-driver shape. | `extract.py:convert_port_sym`, `extract.py:convert_net_sym`, `extract.py:_sym_net_z` | **later**: none for the lifted shapes; the residue needs the x-taint feature or a net-resolution model (multi-driver, tri/wand/wor, undriven bits) [NETRES] |

Xcelium, Verilator and Yosys accept the net form as a continuous driver, Icarus rejects it. | `extract.py:convert_port_sym` | **never**†: P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| `PortSymbol:explicit-expression` | module t (a, .q(y)); input a; output y; logic y; assign y = a; endmodule | An explicit port expression `.q(y)` (IEEE 23.2.1) is legal; slang, Icarus and Xcelium read it with equal values, but Yosys `read_verilog -sv` and Verilator fail on it with a syntax error: a program the scored frontend cannot read, so no score exists for it. | `extract.py:convert_port_sym` | **later**†: The scored frontend reads explicit port expressions (a Yosys / Verilator change, or a different synthesis frontend). The same reasoning as for classes (Thomas, 2026-10-31): legal, out of scope while Yosys `read_verilog -sv` is the frontend. |
| `NetSymbol:<NetKind> (Tri, Tri0, Tri1, WAnd, WOr, TriAnd, TriOr, TriReg, UWire, Supply0, Supply1, Interconnect)` | tri w; wand w; wor w; tri0 / tri1 / triand / trior / trireg / uwire; supply0 gnd; supply1 vcc; interconnect ic; | Explicitly typed nets need driver-set resolution and strength; the explicit-net refusal is a recorded round-2 decision. | `extract.py:convert_net_sym` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: a resolved-net model; supply0 / supply1 (constants) are the cheap first step [NETRES]<br>svGolf: **never**† P-SYNTHESIZABLE |

The analysis pass (`AnalysisManager`) reports `MultipleAlwaysAssigns` (IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2 and 9.2.2.4: another process, an `initial` block included, writes a variable an always_comb/always_ff writes), `MixedVarAssigns` (6.5), `MultipleContAssigns`, `InputPortAssign` (23.3.3.2) and `AlwaysWithoutTimingControl` (9.2.2.1, a simulation deadlock); `Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()` omits all five, and three of them are warnings by slang's definition that the driver promotes to errors. The extractor classifies them by the Driver's own severities (null source location: a `pragma diagnostic` cannot downgrade) and carries each as `SlangAnalysis:<code>` with slang's message. A top with parameters has a verdict per POINT instead (probe sidecar `frontend_errors` / `frontend_analysis`), because the error can depend on the point and the default-point envelope must stay instantiable at a legal one. | `extract.py:_slang_analysis_errors`, `extract.py:_slang_analysis_nodes` | **never**: P-SAME-PROGRAM |
| `SlangError:*` | H: a missing include file (the include directive naming nonexistent.vh) / an unknown macro or directive / import nopkg::*; / a second module of the same sources that reads an undeclared name / any other error in slang's parse, preprocessor or elaboration diagnostics that is not already inside a converted construct | Thomas 2026-10-31 ("if slang reports a program illegal, that is a good reason to reject it") and 2026-11-01 (parse, elaboration and analysis errors alike). Before WP-RB1 an error of the symbolic compilation reached the envelope only when it sat inside a construct the extractor converts (`InvalidExpression`, `VariableSymbol:type`, `ElabSystemTaskSymbol`, ...); a missing `include`, an unknown macro, an unknown package import or an error in another module of the same sources left a CLEAN-LOOKING envelope (identical to the legal program's) and `load_design_sv2` loaded it: a theorem about `X.sem` was then about slang's error RECOVERY of the program, not about the file. The extractor now carries every distinct error of `Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()` as `SlangError:<slang code>` (text `file:line: message`, at most 20, then `SlangError:more`; `SlangError:FrontendFailed` if the list cannot be built), in the top module's `others`, so the design is loud (`hasUnsupported`, no run completes). Same split as `SlangAnalysis:*`: a top without parameters carries them; a top with parameters and a probe sidecar (`--probe-points`) keeps its verdict per POINT (`frontend_errors`: the default-point envelope must stay instantiable where the default point is the illegal one); a top with parameters and no sidecar carries them, since nothing else can vouch for it. Errors of modules the top does not instantiate count (slang diagnoses unused definitions; the analysis pass does not look at them). | `extract.py:_slang_error_nodes`, `extract.py:process_symbolic` | **never**: P-SAME-PROGRAM |

### Parameters, constants and default-point folds

slang folds many constants at the DEFAULT parameter point; emitting that fold would be silently wrong at other points, so the extractor and the Lean constant tier refuse the shapes where default-point and per-point values can differ (the FOLDS lane, [docs/sv-charter.md](sv-charter.md) rounds 3 to 7).

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EnumValueSymbol:default-point-value \| :unsized-literal-member` | an enum whose member values depend on a parameter, or unsized-literal members, used as a value | Member values are slang's default-point constants. | `extract.py:_sym_named_value` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: symbolic enum member values [FOLDS] |
| `VariableSymbol:default-point-array \| :default-point-aggregate \| UnpackedDecl:memory` | logic [7:0] mem [0:K-1] with parameter K; a packed struct whose member width names a parameter | The layout is slang's default-point shape (one decl per default cell, fixed member offsets). Parameter-dependent unpacked declarations are retained as UnpackedDecl, while the flat E store still refuses array-valued state. | `extract.py:_convert_unpacked_decl_sym`, `Param.lean:instDecl` | **later**: array-valued E state [AGGR] |
| `Syntax:<SyntaxKind> \| Syntax:Identifier:<SymbolClass> \| Syntax:Identifier:unresolved` | a packed dimension recovered from syntax: [f(N)-1:0] with a user function, [$high(a):0], [$bits(logic[N-1:0])-1:0] | slang folds declared dimensions without keeping a bound expression, so they are re-read from syntax; unsupported syntax degrades to Unsupported with the resolved width kept. | `extract.py:_syntax_unsupported`, `extract.py:_syntax_name` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: richer syntax recovery [FOLDS] |
| `parameter '<p>' has no declared type and its override is not an integer expression` | an override of an UNTYPED child parameter by an expression outside the INT class (`child #(.P(3'd5))`) | The parameter would take the override's type (IEEE 6.20.2); the constant tier carries integers and would lose it. | `Hier2.lean:PInst.given` | **later**: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: typed override values (a type with each override) in PInst.given / atPoint [FOLDS] (unverified) |

| `parameter arity: got <n>, want <m>` | instantiate called with a different number of arguments than the design has parameters (API misuse) | Positional binding would shift every value. | `Param2.lean:instantiate2From`, `Hier2.lean:PDesign.instantiateRec` | **refused-now** (unverified) |

### always_comb guards and the settle semantics

| tag | trigger | why | where | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AlwaysComb:self-read` | H: always_comb begin y = t; t = a; end / if (c) t = a; y = t; t = b; (a bit read before it is written, written later) | IEEE 9.2.2.2.1(b) leaves any expression the block itself writes out of its implicit sensitivity list, so the LRM's simulation answer for `y = t; t = a;` is deterministic: the block does not re-run on its own write of `t`, and `y` stays one change behind `a`. Icarus 12 and Xcelium 24.03 follow it; Verilator and the Yosys netlist give the settled value (`y = a`). The event-driven simulators and the synthesizers split, so the proof and the score would read different programs. This is NOT an Icarus-only split and NOT LRM nondeterminism. | `CombGuard2.lean:combGuardProc`, `CombGuard2.lean:selfReadMsg`, `Param2.lean:instProcess2`, `Hier2.lean:Process2.inInstance`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2` | **never**: P-NO-SILENT-PICK |
| `AlwaysComb:alias-read` | H: assign w = t; always_comb begin y = w; t = a; end (also assign chains, ~ and slice copies, port loops formed after flattening) | An always_comb reads a bit downstream, through a continuous assign, of a bit it writes at or after the read: Icarus propagates the copy inside the block's run and loses the wake-up (y lags); Xcelium, Verilator, the Yosys netlist and the settle semantics defer it (y = a). Only Icarus differs; IEEE 4.7/4.8 (a procedural statement need not execute as one event, update events may be taken in any order) arguably make Icarus's order legal too. | `CombAlias2.lean:aliasGuardProc`, `CombAlias2.lean:Design2.aliasGuard`, `CombAlias2.lean:PDesign.aliasReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **later**†: Icarus alone is stale; Xcelium, Verilator and the Yosys netlist agree with the settle semantics (class (b)). Two routes, Thomas to pick (NOTE question 2). (A) His Icarus-only ruling applies directly: re-add the two declarations retired in round 6 (iverilog-comb-assign-alias-sensitivity, iverilog-comb-port-loop-sensitivity) on the now-simulated rows and disable AlwaysComb:alias-read for them (plan ICARUS); the model stays settled-only, so Icarus's order, which is arguably LRM-legal, is declared a departure and not a run that binds the golfer. (B) The run-set model (plan NONDET), where the lost-wake-up order is a run. Either way the Xcelium traces must be pinned: the golden file holds 2 of the 7 refused rows (acg_alias_assign, acg_alias_port, left from when they were simulated); chain, not, bits, hier and thru are measured (audit) but unpinned, and xcelium_batch.py pins only SIMULATED rows (a row with a `refusal` is skipped), so the pins arrive with the lift itself. |
| `Clock:source` | H: logic clk; always_ff @(posedge clk) y <= a & b; (undriven) / assign clk = 1'b0; ... (tied) / assign g = clk & en; always_ff @(posedge g) ... (gated) / always_ff @(posedge div) with div a register / a clock that is an output or an internal net | Sem2 runs every edge process once per cycle and never reads the clock's value, so it is exact only when the clock is a one-bit INPUT port of the top whose edge is the cycle. A dead, tied, gated, derived, register or internal-net clock captures every cycle in the model and never (or only on enabled edges) in a simulator: measured on Xcelium 24.03 and Icarus 12.0 (rows clk_undriven, clk_tied, clk_gated, clk_internal, clk_reg). | `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockSourceViol`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.clockViolation`, `ClockGuard2.lean:Design2.disciplineGuard`, `ClockGuard2.lean:PDesign.clockReport`, `Ingest2.lean:load_design_sv2`, `runner2.lean:main` | **later**: clock edges as events (S5): edge detection from the clock signal between snapshots, clock gating, derived clocks (a clock produced by NBA logic also needs the R1 slot loop) [SEQ] |

Measured: a true oscillator hangs Icarus, aborts Verilator ("did not converge") and ends at an arbitrary value in Xcelium, so there is no value for the tools to agree on, and such a design can never satisfy `Terminates2`. A loop that SETTLES is not this row: run2 completes it (mux feedback, SR latch, a structural loop computing a = b = d, and `assign a = ~a`, which settles at x). | `kinds chosen at run time (helper-built tags)` | the `flag` helper of _sym_xz_literal_scan, _sym_unsized_xz_widening, _sym_constant_label_refusal, _convert_incdec's context tag | These call sites forward a tag computed by a helper; the concrete tags (IntegerLiteral:unsized-xz-parametric, ConversionExpression:xz-literal-parametric, CallExpression:unsized-xz-cast, ...) belong to the rows of the family they come from. | `extract.py:_sym_xz_literal_scan`, `extract.py:_sym_unsized_xz_widening`, `extract.py:_sym_constant_label_refusal`, `extract.py:_convert_incdec` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `ExtractorInternal:<PythonException>` | an extractor bug (none constructed) | Defensive: the extractor failed on a node and emits a loud Unsupported rather than aborting. Any occurrence is a bug to fix. | `extract.py:internal_error` | **refused-now** (unverified) |
| `M0-tier refusals (the self-check path, schema sv-0.1)` | about 260 unsupported() sites reachable only in non-symbolic (--single-file) mode | Not part of the ls-sv load path: the M0 tier is the self-check extractor. `python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check` prints the current count and requires nothing of them. | `extract.py:process_file`, `extract.py:_convert_design` | **refused-now** |

## Declared departures (not refusals)

These are admitted and DIFFER from a simulator on purpose; each is a hash-bound row in `harness/sv/cases2.json`.

| departure | what differs | source |
|---|---|---|
| Run-time-base part select partly out of range | `v[sel +: 4]` with a signal base keeps the LRM value (in-range bits kept, x elsewhere); Xcelium returns all x. Declared as Xcelium-sim oracle_disagreement rows (partsel_dyn*, dyn32_part). Reason for declaring rather than refusing is not stated in the sources (unverified). | svgolf/PLAN.md Round 6; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 1, 6.4 |
| Cross-process bit splits | acg_xproc_bits (LRM-legal; Icarus-only departure, stays declared). | docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 9 |
| Icarus compiler assertions / vvp aborts | Icarus 'unavailable' rows are declared, not refused. | docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md 'Unavailable oracles' |
| String literal escapes \a \v \f | Xcelium 24.03 reads each of the named control escapes of IEEE 1800-2023 Table 5-1 as the plain letter (a, v, f); slang, Icarus 12, Verilator 5.042 and Yosys 0.53 produce 7, 11 and 12, which the model keeps. Admitted, not refused (Thomas 2026-11-01); declared as the Xcelium-sim oracle_disagreement row lit_str_ctl (declaration xcelium-named-control-escape-letters, XREF-DECLARED), control row lit_str_ctl_ok. | docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md 'String literal escapes `\a \v \f`'; docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md sections 4 and 6 |

## Known holes: admitted today, not refused

A register of refusals cannot list what nobody refuses. These are the shapes the audits found that the tier ADMITS although a tool disagrees; none has been decided.

| hole | what | source |
|---|---|---|
| Shift counts wider than 32 bits | Xcelium truncates a shift count silently and nothing refuses it. (Bit-select indexes are refused, Select:wide-index, including the index of a run-time unpacked-array element where the extractor admits one (the lane-A verifier's probe wi_arr), and part-select bases are refused as RangeSelectExpression:dynamic-wide-base.) | docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.4 |
| PortConn:net-width narrower than the verified rule | full-range part-select or constant bit-select of a net actual, signed net, another instance's output net, tri1 formal, the net-collapse effect of a second mismatched connection and the OUTPUT-direction twin are still admitted. | LeanModels/Sv/Hier2.lean docstring; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 7 |
| Self-read guard on the M0 family | PDesign.instantiateD (M0) is not covered by the self-read guard (reachable only at a non-default point of a parametric self-reading body). | docs/sv-charter.md WP4 Gaps |
| Cross-process bit splits | acg_xproc_bits, x_dyn, x_child are admitted (LRM-legal, Icarus-only departure; only one is a declared row). | docs/sv-charter.md round 4 |
| Guards beside name.sem | a forall-N proof about `name.sem` at a point no consumer checks is not covered by the loader-side guards. | LeanModels/Sv/RangeGuard2.lean header |
| x/z digits inside a casez/casex item EXPRESSION (svGolf gate) | x/z digits are exempt anywhere inside a casez/casex item, not only as the item's own literal; `casez (a[1:0]) (a[0] == 1'bz) ? 2'b00 : 2'b01: ...` passes the gate (svgolf/score/tests/gate/casez_expr.sv). Whether ls-sv and Yosys then differ was not measured. | svgolf/score/srcgate.py (xz_literal_findings); measured by the register authors |
| slang's driver: what the analysis-pass rule still does not read | The analysis-pass errors (`multiple-always-assigns`, `mixed-var-assigns`, `multiple-cont-assigns`, "cannot assign to input port", "'always' procedure does not advance time") ARE read since 2026-11-01 (policy "slang reports a program illegal"). What it does not read, measured on the committed corpora with the Driver's own severities: (1) the elaboration-time warnings that the driver promotes to errors (`IndexOOB`, `RangeOOB`, `DynamicNotProcedural`, `UnknownSystemName`, ...: 175 diagnostic codes have another severity in the Driver's engine than in a bare DiagnosticEngine, 41 of them promoted from warning to error and 134 switched off): they are NOT errors for the extractor, because 9 envelopes with `IndexOOB`, 9 with `RangeOOB` and 1 with `DynamicNotProcedural` (of the 1271 committed envelopes) are admitted differential rows that read x for the out-of-range select, Xcelium-pinned; for svGolf `fourstate`'s rule (c) already refuses the out-of-range ones as x sources, and the 4 svGolf corpus files with such a code (const_oob_write, param_oob, unique_rare, host_dump) are refused by other rules; promoting them is a policy choice, not a measurement; (2) the extractor's M0 single-file mode (`process_file`, sv-0.1): 3 committed M0 envelopes hold an analysis error (always_comb_written_excluded, always_no_control_refuse, multiple_variable_continuous_drivers) and are conformance-lane designs, untouched; (3) a parametric top's default-point envelope carries no analysis marker, and since WP-RB1 no `SlangError` marker when `--probe-points` was given (the verdict is per point, the probe sidecar), so a consumer that instantiates a parametric envelope at a point no sidecar covers relies on the Lean `driversOk` guard (svGolf always probes the scoring point); (4) a task with an EMPTY banlist skips the banlist front check (`banlist.check` returns early), so `fourstate` is the only svGolf stage that reads slang's analysis errors there; (5) `srcgate.py` parses without elaborating and has no analysis to read; (6) the analysis reads the design's own hierarchy, as the other stages do: an uninstantiated module with an analysis error is not refused (the slang CLI would); parse and elaboration errors, by contrast, are read over the whole compilation since WP-RB1 (row sa-slang-error), an uninstantiated module's undeclared name included. | docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md section 5; svgolf/score/slangdriver.py; extractors/sv/test_slang_analysis.py; measured by WP-R-D 2026-11-01 (harness: scratchpad measure.py over Examples/system-verilog and svgolf); extractors/sv/test_slang_errors.py |
| Host access from the Lean file of a submission (svGolf) | MITIGATED by the checker's sandbox (WP-S, 2026-10-31); not gated. The source gate's host-access rule (`P-NO-HOST-ACCESS`) covers the SystemVerilog text. A Solution.lean is compiled and elaborated with the checker's privileges and `import Lean` (since WP-B, Mathlib) is allowed: before the sandbox, a reference solution with an added `#eval IO.FS.readFile "/etc/hosts"` and an `IO.FS.writeFile` was ACCEPTED (stage done), read the file, wrote another one, and what the `#eval` printed came back in `stages.solution.messages`; the same file read the competition salt `SVGOLF_POSTSYNTH_SALT` out of the checker's environment (with it a player precomputes the post-synthesis vectors), opened a TCP connection (Lean core has sockets, no program is spawned), replaced the trusted `Design.olean` through a hard link and spawned `/bin/sh`. A scan of the Lean file cannot stop that (the shipped references use a local `elab` and macros; Lean metaprograms reach IO under many names; `unsafe` code makes the interpreter untrusted). The mitigation is a sandbox around every process that runs submitted text: `check.py --sandbox {off,auto,require}` (default auto; `leaderboard.py add`/`verify` use `require`), macOS Seatbelt or Linux bubblewrap, a canary self-test at every start, no network, reads only of the inputs, writes only of one fresh output directory, no other program, a scrubbed environment, limits enforced from outside; tests/run.py step `sandbox` pins the attacks. RESIDUAL: (1) on a machine without a mechanism `auto` runs unsandboxed and says so (`require` refuses); (2) a hostile file that catches its errors is accepted, neutralized; (3) the existence, size and times of any path are visible (global file-read-metadata, for speed); (4) the parsers that run in the checker's own process (pyslang in the source gate, the banlist and fourstate front checks) are not sandboxed: moving them into one sandboxed worker is the recorded next step; (5) a crafted .olean is loaded by the comparator and leanchecker, which also run inside the sandbox, with the kernel replay as the check; (6) kernel and Seatbelt bugs, what system.sb grants every Apple command-line program; (7) Linux was validated at the self-test and process level (Rocky 9.8, bwrap 0.6.3), not yet with Lean. | svgolf/README.md Sandbox and Checker v0 limits; svgolf/check/sandbox/; measured by the register authors and by WP-S |

## Data format

- entries[] (ls-sv tier) and svgolf.entries[] (svGolf checker) share one record shape:
- id (unique slug), tag (display name; `Family:detail` where the code has one), group, layers (extractor | lean-model | lean-guard | lean-loader | lean-proof-tooling | svgolf-*), trigger (a measured source, `H:` = the body of the standard test module), why, category (refused-now | later | never | refused-pending), proposed (true = not confirmed by Thomas), decided_by (the recorded decision), since (date, when known).
- later: prerequisite (required) and plan (a plan_items id); never: principle (required, from the principle table); refused-pending: decided_by or source (the decision) and kinds that may be absent from the code.
- svgolf (optional, on an ls-sv entry): {category, principle | prerequisite, proposed}: the status for a svGolf submission when it differs from the ls-sv status.
- kinds.extractor / kinds.lean: the code tags the row covers (exact strings; `glob:<pattern>` for a deliberate family; `@default:<function>` for an extractor site that takes the slang class name; a bare `*` for a site whose whole kind is built at run time). The completeness check requires every live code tag to be covered and every listed tag to exist.
- match: [{file, text}]: for a refusal that has only a message, the text must still be found in the file. where: [{file, fn}]: the function that raises it (line numbers are resolved by --where, never stored). attacks: svgolf only, `task/name` of every tests/expected.json design the row explains.
- evidence (where it is documented), unverified (read from the source, never triggered by a run), verified_by_run, notes, value_rank / value_note (the ordering of the 'Allowed later' table), aggregate (svGolf only: a summary row hidden from svgolf/REFUSALS.md).

## Keeping this file true

`python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check` fails when the extractor or the Lean code raises a tagged refusal that is not listed here, when a listed tag has disappeared from the code, or when this file is stale. After round-6 style work: rerun `--check`, add the new rows to `docs/sv-refusals.json`, run `--write`. A checkout without `svgolf/` (the svGolf project lives on the golf branch) is checked for this half only: `--check` says it skipped the svGolf half and `--write` regenerates this file alone.
